samples.summary: `api-keys` commands bypass `send()`, so the SESSION_EXPIRED/refresh invariant this delta asserts does not hold for them
samples.evidence: The delta routes `api-keys create/list/revoke` (api-keys.ts:22,36,50) through `forwardUpstreamError`, and the new comment in formatter.ts:153-158 plus the new test cases (upstream-error.test.ts:242-244) assert the invariant "every command that talks to the backend" reports the same code, "the client's own 401 SESSION_EXPIRED most of all". But `listApiKeys` (http-client.ts:365-371), `createApiKey` (372-382) and `revokeApiKey` (383-389) call `fetch` directly instead of `this.send(...)`: they never attempt `refreshSession()` on a 401 and never synthesize `sessionExpiredBody()`. Under JWT auth an expired access token on these three commands (a) is not retried after a refresh that would have succeeded — the command fails where every other command succeeds — and (b) surfaces the raw server 401 body, which `forwardUpstreamError` reports as `HTTP_ERROR`, not `SESSION_EXPIRED`. The code an agent branches on therefore still depends on which subcommand it ran, which is exactly the bug this change claims to close; the new tests do not catch it because the fetch stub never exercises the 401/refresh path.

samples.summary: `api-keys revoke` prints `null` on a successful empty-body (204) response
samples.evidence: `revokeApiKey` does `await res.json().catch(() => null)` (http-client.ts:387-388), so a 204/empty body yields `data === null` with `ok === true`. The touched success path at api-keys.ts:51 then calls `output(null, opts.format)`, printing the literal `null` (or throwing/emitting an empty table under `--format table|csv`) instead of a result body. Same pattern applies to `docs/notes/slides/files delete` if the backend answers 204.

samples.summary: Two of the sites changed in this delta (`sheets cells batch`, `sheets import`) are absent from the new parametrized CASES list
samples.evidence: The delta converts `cells.ts:147` (`sheets cells batch`) and `sheets-import.ts:91` (`sheets import`) to `forwardUpstreamError`, but the new CASES array (upstream-error.test.ts:211-245) enumerates every other converted command and omits these two. `sheets cells batch` reads stdin when `--data` is absent and `sheets import` reads a file, so their error paths have extra preconditions and are precisely the ones most likely to regress un-noticed.
searchedFor: grep for 'batch' and 'import' in packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts CASES

samples.summary: Auth/network failures now exit 1 from ~20 more commands, contradicting the documented exit-code mapping
samples.evidence: `forwardUpstreamError` sets `process.exitCode = 1` for every failed upstream response, including the client-synthesized 401 `SESSION_EXPIRED` envelope (http-client.ts:157-164). README.md:127-128 documents `2` for "system error (network, auth)". The delta routes every remaining command through this single path, so the mismatch is now the behavior of the whole CLI rather than six commands, and an agent branching on exit status cannot distinguish an auth failure from a user error.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: `listApiKeys` (http-client.ts:365-371), `createApiKey` (372-382) and `revokeApiKey` (383-389) call `fetch` directly rather than `this.send(...)` (133-154), so they never attempt `refreshSession()` (90-126) on a 401 and never synthesize `sessionExpiredBody()` (157-164). All three api-keys subcommands funnel `!res.ok` into `forwardUpstreamError` (api-keys.ts:22,36,50), which only forwards a documented envelope and otherwise throws `UpstreamHttpError` with `code = 'HTTP_ERROR'` (formatter.ts:137-146,173-178) — so a raw server 401 surfaces as HTTP_ERROR, not SESSION_EXPIRED, contradicting the invariant asserted at formatter.ts:153-158 and the client contract documented at config/config.ts:71-73. No caller-side guard exists: `getClient` (commands/root.ts:38-40) simply constructs the client with no proactive refresh, and `isExpired` is only used for display (commands/status.ts:30). Real, on a live JWT path, and in the correctness lane (missing retry/refresh + broken error-contract invariant).

finding.summary: New envelope-forwarding helper is not applied to the many other command sites, which still discard a real backend envelope (e.g. SESSION_EXPIRED) as `{code:"ERROR"}`
finding.evidence: `forwardUpstreamError`/`upstreamErrorJson` are wired into only 6 command sites (docs/notes/slides content+export) and the import/upload/download orchestrators. Every other site still does `if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`)` — docs.ts:80,107,121,139,157; notes.ts:40,67,81,99,117; slides.ts:45,72,86,104,122; cells.ts:25,65,91,143; tabs.ts:16,49,75; files.ts:86,106,124,142; api-keys.ts:18,32,46. That path throws away the response body entirely, including bodies that *are* the documented envelope: `HttpClient.sessionExpiredBody()` (http-client.ts:157) returns `{error:{code:'SESSION_EXPIRED',message:'Session expired. Run `wafflebase login`.'}}` with `ok:false, status:401` (http-client.ts:181), so `wafflebase docs get <id>` on an expired JWT session emits `{error:{code:"ERROR",message:"HTTP 401"}}` and the actionable `code` an agent is supposed to branch on is lost. Same for any backend envelope on those endpoints. The change makes the CLI's error contract depend on which subcommand was run, which is exactly what the new helper's doc comment says must not happen.

verdict.reason: The presence claim is false in this working tree. The finding says the envelope helper is wired into only 6 sites and that docs.ts:80,107,121,139,157; notes.ts:40,67,81,99,117; slides.ts:45,72,86,104,122; cells.ts; tabs.ts; files.ts; api-keys.ts still do `throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`)`. Reading each file, every one of those call sites is `if (!res.ok) return forwardUpstreamError(res);` and every file imports forwardUpstreamError from ../output/formatter.js (docs.ts:7, tabs.ts:3-7, api-keys.ts:3-7, cells.ts:6, files.ts:6, notes.ts:7, slides.ts:7). A repo-wide grep for "HTTP ${" in packages/cli/src returns only formatter.ts:126 (inside the helper's own upstreamMessage) and login.ts:98 (an unrelated user-facing message) — no surviving bare `HTTP <status>` throw exists in the CLI. The specific SESSION_EXPIRED scenario cited is therefore unreachable: docs.ts:121 hands the 401 body to forwardUpstreamError, which detects the documented envelope and prints it verbatim (formatter.ts:173-177). The "six sites" figure comes from the helper's own doc comment describing the prior state ("It used to be six sites, with the rest throwing new Error(\"HTTP <status>\")", formatter.ts:153-158), which the reviewer appears to have read as current. Line numbers in the finding are also uniformly ~4 lines stale relative to the working tree, consistent with reading the pre-change revision.
